---
title: Collect missing inputs
description: Pause for typed values, retain the workflow position, and resume the same request.
---

`requestInput()` gives missing information an explicit `awaiting_input` state.
It belongs in a dedicated collection tool; the actual query runs after the
inputs have arrived. It is data collection, separate from `checkIn` and
middleware `ask`, which collect approval decisions.

`InputRequestDeclaration` is the collection tool's declaration; each `InputField`
names a supported `InputValue` type and optional choices. `AwaitingInput` is its
runtime projection with accepted values, missing fields and workflow origin.
`isInputPause` narrows a run result to the typed input arm. An `InputResponse`
supplies values, while `InputCancellation` explicitly ends a hosted request.
A complete response becomes an `InputResponseResult` in the original tool's
result slot. `InputRequestError` rejects malformed declarations or replies with
`ERR_INPUT_REQUEST_INVALID`; it does not consume the paused checkpoint.

```ts
import { Agent, defineTool, requestInput, isInputPause } from 'agentfootprint';
import { mock } from 'agentfootprint/providers';

const collect = defineTool({
  name: 'collect_window',
  description: 'Collect the timezone needed to interpret the query window.',
  inputSchema: { type: 'object', properties: {} },
  execute: () => requestInput({
    id: 'query-window',
    question: 'Which timezone should this window use?',
    fields: [
      { id: 'year', type: 'number', required: false },
      { id: 'timezone', type: 'string', description: 'An IANA timezone or UTC.' },
    ],
    supplied: { year: 2026 },
    context: { operation: 'query_records', yearPolicy: 'application-default' },
  }),
});

const agent = Agent.create({ provider: mock({ replies: [
  { toolCalls: [{ id: 'input-1', name: 'collect_window', args: {} }] },
  { content: 'The inputs are ready for the query.' },
] }), model: 'mock' }).tool(collect).build();

const asked = await agent.run({ message: 'Inspect the requested window.' });
if (isInputPause(asked)) {
  await agent.resume(asked.checkpoint, {
    requestId: asked.awaitingInput.requestId,
    values: { timezone: 'UTC' },
  });
}
```

The example year is an author-supplied value, not a library date default.
The application owns date, timezone, site and other domain policies.
`context` holds bounded JSON metadata from the collection tool. The answer
cannot replace it. Domain validation, such as whether a timezone exists,
belongs to that application's adapter; the library validates field types,
declared choices, unknown fields and the matching request token.

When a lookup does raise about its own miss (the dedicated collection tool
stays the documented shape), it still declares what it looked at: pass the
envelope `absent()` returns as `absence`. It is filed when the request is
raised, before the checkpoint — the same `tools.absent` event and
`coverageDeclared` row that `absent(…)`, returned, would file. It never enters
the pending value and nothing reads it on resume, so say the miss in
`question` if the person should hear it now. A value the absence recognizer
cannot read is refused when the request is raised (`absence: null` is the
field omitted); an envelope whose lists cannot be read errors the call instead
of pausing, as it would returned. The paused call is answered by the person,
so it is never delivered an `'absent'` status.

Fields accept `string`, finite `number`, or `boolean`, optional `description`
and optional `enum`. Fields are required unless `required: false`. There are
at most 32 fields; strings and descriptions are bounded to 4096 characters,
choice lists to 100 values, and context to 16384 JSON characters.
At least one required field must be missing to request input; when all are
already known, the collecting tool should continue without raising a pause.

The pending value contains `missing`, `supplied`, and `origins`. Origins are
`declaration` for values the collecting tool supplied and `response` for values
accepted from a reply. Runtime-stamped `origin` identifies the original
request, tool call, selected skill and any outstanding skill candidates.
This is workflow context, not evidence that a collector observed those values.

Partial answers return another input pause without a model call, query or
step advance. Persist the returned checkpoint: it contains the newly accepted
values. A complete answer becomes the collecting tool's result:

```ts
{
  status: 'input_received',
  requestId: 'runtime-generated-token',
  values: { year: 2026, timezone: 'UTC' },
  origins: { year: 'declaration', timezone: 'response' },
  context: { operation: 'query_records', yearPolicy: 'application-default' },
  origin: { originalRequest: 'Inspect the requested window.', toolCallId: 'input-1' }
}
```

The existing result middleware, placement, redaction and size limits still
process that result. The collection tool is not executed again. A complete
FlowchartCheckpoint retains the selected skill, history and step position
across a process restart; the resuming agent must mount the same chart.
Invalid or stale replies leave the checkpoint available for correction.
`describedResult({ clarify: ... })` remains an informational result and does not
automatically pause a run.

## When the library asks — a tool's `ask` rule

A collection tool is the shape for a question only your app can frame (a
calendar date, a year and a timezone together). For a single ARGUMENT only the
person can give — the period a log search covers, the site a report is for —
declare it on the tool that takes it, and the library asks for you:

<CodeFile path="examples/features/75-ask-for-missing-arguments.ts" region="ask-for-missing-arguments" title="examples/features/75-ask-for-missing-arguments.ts (region: ask-for-missing-arguments)" />

When a batch of calls leaves `window` out, nothing in the batch runs. The run
pauses on ONE typed input for everything the batch needs — the same
`isInputPause` / `awaitingInput` / `resume` shape as above, and `standingAgent`
renders, answers and cancels it like any other:

<CodeFile path="examples/features/75-ask-for-missing-arguments.ts" region="the-ask" title="examples/features/75-ask-for-missing-arguments.ts (region: the-ask)" />

- **One field per argument, bound to every call that needs it.** Field ids are
  positional (`f1`, `f2`, …). Each field's `description` is the tool author's
  question and its `enum` the author's choices; the question itself is a fixed
  library sentence. `awaitingInput.context.agentfootprint` —
  `{ ask: 'arguments', fields: [{ id, tool, argument, calls }] }` — says what
  each field is for; `origin.toolCallId` names the batch's first asked call.
- **Nothing the model proposed rides the ask.** No value it wrote, no choice.
- **One period, one question.** Two tools whose period arguments are spelled
  differently (`24h` and `-24h`) share one field when their choices are the
  same periods; each call runs with the answer in its own spelling.
- **The answer is re-checked** against the tool's own schema for that argument
  (an integer answered `2.5`, a string that breaks its `pattern`). An answer
  that does not fit is asked again with a second fixed question — at most three
  times; then the calls that needed it are refused, and the model reads why.
- **The resume adds no model call.** Each call runs on its ordinary path —
  permission, middleware, validation — with the answer filled in, and its
  result tells the model the value was the person's answer. `agent.findings()`
  holds an `argument` row `asked: 'missing'` per value (from the moment of the
  ask), then `source: 'answered'` (`free: true` for a free-text field).
  `agent.assessment()` reads **ask** while the question is out.
- **One human question per resume — and the answer is kept.** In the batch that
  asked, a later call that would need a person — its check-in, a middleware
  `ask`, a credential consent, the tool's own `requestInput` — is refused by name
  instead of pausing a second time. When that call carried the person's answers,
  they are kept for the rest of the turn and the model is told so: proposed
  again with the argument left out, the call runs with the kept answer (nobody
  is asked again) and pauses for its own step then. A tool with both an `ask`
  rule and a check-in costs the person two round trips. A kept answer is used
  once; a later call of the same tool in another batch is asked again.
- **A credential consent in the batch that asked** (under the default
  `onAuthorizationRequired: 'pause'`): the model reads the credential's own
  refusal, and if the turn ends without a later call obtaining the credential,
  the turn raises `CredentialConsentRequiredError` — carrying the authorization
  URL to your app — instead of returning the model's answer.
- **The resume event keeps the answer out.** The `agentfootprint.pause.resume`
  event of this ask carries the reply's shape — its request id and field ids —
  with every value read as `'REDACTED'`, because an answer may fill an argument
  the tool's own view hides; the `answered` rows carry what each tool's view
  allows.
- **A value the model did send** runs as sent and is recorded as the model's
  own — the library does not ask about it, unless declared sources are on (next
  section).

Your app can keep its own state on the ask (a routing step, a screen id):
`Agent.create({ …, argumentAskContext: () => ({ routing: { step: 'metrics' } }) })`
spreads the object into `context` beside the library's key, which it may not use.

## Where each value came from — declared sources

With `.findings({ argumentSources: true })`, the model says, for each argument of
a ruled call, where the value came from — the person's words (copied as a
`quote`), a tool result (its `id`), the person's earlier answer, the app's own
text, or `'assumed'` — and the library **checks** each claim before anything in
the batch runs. A choice can carry words you vouch for as meaning it
(`{ value: '7d', said: ['last week'] }`), so "over the last week" checks out as
`7d` without the library ever parsing a time phrase:

<CodeFile path="examples/features/76-declared-sources.ts" region="declared-sources" title="examples/features/76-declared-sources.ts (region: declared-sources)" />

<CodeFile path="examples/features/76-declared-sources.ts" region="checked" title="examples/features/76-declared-sources.ts (region: checked)" />

- **A checked value runs.** The quote must be in the person's own messages, and
  the value in the quote or one of your phrases for it; a result id must name a
  result the model was served, and the value must be in that result's own bytes
  (a note the library added never counts); an earlier answer must be the
  person's answer to the library's ask. The row says what was checked:
  `source: 'said'` with `matched: 'phrase'`, `'result'`, `'answered'`, `'app'`.
- **An unchecked value on an `ask` argument is asked** — nothing declared, a
  failed claim, or a READING (the words are the person's, the value is not in
  them). The ask shows the person their own words (`quoted`), never the model's
  value; the answer replaces it, and the row keeps the model's value as
  `proposed`.
- **A failed claim is recorded as written**, never repaired
  (`failed: 'quote-not-found'`, `'not-in-result'`, …), and the answer's standing
  says the value is not traced.
- **Checked is not verified.** Matching words cannot see a negation or another
  sentence, so a checked value keeps a reason from firing and supports nothing:
  the answer reads "consistent with the record", never "known".
- **Another runner's message is not the person's.** `Sequence`, `Loop`,
  `workflow()` and `graph()` mark a step's (or node's) message that is an earlier
  one's output, and a quote from it fails; code that composes runners by hand
  passes `messageFrom: 'composed'` to `run()`.
- **A quote stays off the record while a tool hides arguments.** A quote is the
  person's free text and may hold a value another tool keeps out of the record
  (a password given in the same sentence), so on an agent with such a tool
  (`flowchartAsTool({ redact })`) every row's `quote` reads `'REDACTED'` and the
  ask shows no `quoted` — the check itself still runs.
- **It costs tokens, and it is off by default.** The `from` property rides only on
  tools that declare `askOrAssume`, plus one instruction line. It needs the inputs
  layer and is refused at build without it.

## Hosted chat

`standingAgent` stores the paused run under its session and returns its usual
`awaiting` response, with `awaiting.awaitingInput` for this arm. The checkpoint
stays on the server. The existing generic `decision` transport also carries
data replies:

```json
{ "input": "", "sessionId": "current-session", "decision": { "requestId": "runtime-generated-token", "values": { "timezone": "UTC" } } }
```

Reload the current question without a model call:

`SESSION_PENDING_OP`, exported by `agentfootprint/hosting`, names this read-only
operation in the shared transport grammar.

```json
{ "op": "session-pending", "sessionId": "current-session" }
```

The response is `{ pending: PendingAsk | null }`. It uses the same session
ownership rule as invoking the session, and returns no checkpoint or transcript.
Cancelling is explicit:

```json
{ "input": "", "sessionId": "current-session", "decision": { "requestId": "runtime-generated-token", "cancel": true } }
```

Hosted cancellation records `input_cancelled`, closes the pending input request
and retains the conversation. Run-scoped resources for that session are released;
session-scoped resources and other paused sessions remain open. This happens
without calling a model or running remaining
tools. It applies only to this data-collection arm, never a consent gate.
Direct runner users use `abandonPause()` before starting another request;
discard the old checkpoint if it must no longer be resumable. If resources were
registered under a hosting session, end the abandoned turn explicitly with
`await agent.closeToolSessions({ scope: 'run', sessionId })`.
An ordinary message does not implicitly approve, cancel, or supply typed fields.
